entry.gloss: the five lines music is written on
entry.def: Five horizontal lines and the four spaces between them. Notes are written on the lines and in the spaces; higher notes sound higher. Also called a stave.

entry.gloss: sign that fixes the notes of the staff
entry.def: A sign at the start of the staff that names one line, and so every line and space. The treble clef marks G4 and the bass clef marks F3.

entry.gloss: clef for higher notes; its curl marks the second line
entry.def: The clef whose curl wraps around the second line, marking it as G4, so it is also called the G clef. It is used for higher instruments and voices and for the right hand of piano music.

entry.gloss: clef for lower notes; its dots mark the fourth line
entry.def: The clef whose two dots sit on either side of the fourth line, marking it as F3, so it is also called the F clef. It is used for lower instruments and voices and for the left hand of piano music.

entry.gloss: treble and bass staves joined by a brace
entry.def: A treble staff above a bass staff, joined at the left by a brace and a line. It is used for piano music; middle C lies between the two staves. Called the great stave in British English.

entry.gloss: short extra line above or below the staff
entry.def: A short line that extends the staff for a single note that lies above or below it. Each ledger line continues the pattern of lines and spaces.

entry.gloss: the note between the treble and bass staves
entry.def: The C near the middle of the piano keyboard, C4 in scientific pitch notation. It is written on the first ledger line below the treble staff or above the bass staff.

entry.gloss: distance to the next note with the same letter name
entry.def: The interval between a note and the next higher or lower note with the same letter, such as C4 and C5. The higher note vibrates exactly twice as fast, so the two sound alike.

entry.gloss: play an octave higher or lower than written
entry.def: The sign 8va with a dashed line above the staff means that the notes under the line sound an octave higher than written; 8vb or 8va bassa below the staff means an octave lower. It saves many ledger lines.

entry.gloss: how long a note lasts compared with others
entry.def: The length of a note in relation to other notes, shown by its shape. Each common value is half the one before: whole, half, quarter, eighth and sixteenth note. How long a value lasts in seconds depends on the tempo.

figure.staff: A4/w | A4/h A4/h | A4/q A4/q A4/q A4/q | A4/e A4/e A4/e A4/e A4/e A4/e A4/e A4/e |.
figure.caption: One whole note, two half notes, four quarter notes and eight eighth notes fill the same time.

entry.gloss: the oval part of a note
entry.def: The oval part of a note, written on a line or in a space to show the pitch. Whole and half notes have hollow noteheads; quarter notes and shorter values have filled ones.

entry.gloss: vertical line attached to a notehead
entry.def: The thin vertical line attached to the notehead of every note shorter than a whole note. Notes below the middle line of the staff have stems going up on the right; notes above it have stems going down on the left, and notes on the middle line usually do too.

entry.gloss: curved tail at the end of a stem
entry.def: A curved tail at the end of the stem of a single short note, always on the right of the stem. An eighth note has one flag and a sixteenth note two; each flag halves the value.

entry.gloss: thick line joining the stems of short notes
entry.def: A thick line that joins the stems of eighth notes and shorter values into groups, usually one group per beat. Eighth notes have one beam and sixteenth notes two, just as they would have one or two flags.

figure.staff: A4/e B4/e C5/e D5/e | E5/s D5/s C5/s B4/s A4/s B4/s C5/s A4/s |.

entry.gloss: hollow note without a stem: four quarter notes
entry.def: A note with a hollow notehead and no stem, as long as two half notes or four quarter notes. In 4/4 time it fills a whole bar. Called a semibreve in British English.

entry.gloss: hollow note with a stem: two quarter notes
entry.def: A note with a hollow notehead and a stem, half as long as a whole note and as long as two quarter notes. Called a minim in British English.

entry.gloss: filled note with a stem: one beat in 4/4
entry.def: A note with a filled notehead and a stem, a quarter of a whole note. In 2/4, 3/4 and 4/4 time it lasts one beat. Called a crotchet in British English.

entry.gloss: note with one flag or beam: half a quarter note
entry.def: A note with a filled notehead, a stem and one flag, or one beam when grouped; two eighth notes last as long as a quarter note. Called a quaver in British English.

entry.gloss: note with two flags or beams: a quarter of a quarter note
entry.def: A note with two flags, or two beams when grouped; four sixteenth notes last as long as a quarter note. Called a semiquaver in British English.

figure.staff: A4/s r/s r/e A4/s B4/s C5/s D5/s |.

entry.gloss: a measured silence
entry.def: A sign for silence that lasts as long as a note value. Every note value has a matching rest, and a dot lengthens a rest as it does a note.

figure.staff: r/w | r/h r/q r/e r/s r/s |.
figure.caption: A whole rest, then a half, a quarter, an eighth and two sixteenth rests.

entry.gloss: block hanging from the fourth line
entry.def: A rest as long as a whole note: a small block hanging below the fourth line of the staff. It also marks a whole bar of rest in any time signature. Called a semibreve rest in British English.

figure.caption: A whole rest fills a bar of 3/4 as well.

entry.gloss: block sitting on the middle line
entry.def: A rest as long as a half note: a small block sitting on the middle line of the staff. Called a minim rest in British English.

entry.gloss: zigzag rest worth a quarter note
entry.def: A rest as long as a quarter note, drawn as a vertical zigzag. Called a crotchet rest in British English.

entry.gloss: rest with one hook: half a quarter rest
entry.def: A rest as long as an eighth note, drawn as a slanted stroke with one hook. Called a quaver rest in British English.

entry.gloss: rest with two hooks: a quarter of a quarter rest
entry.def: A rest as long as a sixteenth note, drawn as a slanted stroke with two hooks. Called a semiquaver rest in British English.

figure.staff: r/s A4/s A4/s A4/s r/s A4/s A4/s A4/s |.

entry.gloss: adds half the value of the note
entry.def: A dot after a note or rest makes it half as long again: a dotted half note lasts three quarter notes, and a dotted quarter note three eighth notes. A dot above or below a notehead is a different sign, staccato.

figure.caption: A dotted half note fills a bar of 3/4; a dotted quarter note and an eighth note fill two beats.

entry.gloss: curve joining two notes of the same pitch into one
entry.def: A curved line joining two neighboring notes of the same pitch: the second note is not played again, so the two sound as one note lasting their combined value. Ties are needed to carry a note across a barline.

figure.staff: C5/q D5/q E5/h~ | E5/q D5/q C5/h |.
figure.caption: The tie carries the E across the barline: it lasts three beats.

entry.gloss: a group of beats between two barlines
entry.def: A unit of musical time holding the number of beats that the time signature gives, marked off by barlines. Called a measure in American English.

figure.staff: G4/q A4/q B4/q | C5/h B4/q | A4/h. |.
figure.caption: Three bars of 3/4, each holding three quarter-note beats.

entry.gloss: vertical line that ends a bar
entry.def: A vertical line through the staff that separates one bar from the next. An accidental lasts until the next barline.

entry.gloss: two thin lines that end a section
entry.def: Two thin barlines close together. They mark the end of a section, often where the key signature or time signature changes.

entry.gloss: thin and thick line that ends a piece
entry.def: A thin line followed by a thick line, marking the end of a piece or movement.

entry.gloss: double barline with two dots: play the passage again
entry.def: A double barline with two dots beside it. The music between a start-repeat sign (dots after the lines) and an end-repeat sign (dots before them) is played twice; if there is no start-repeat sign, repeat from the beginning.

entry.gloss: numbered brackets: different endings for a repeat
entry.def: Brackets numbered 1 and 2 over the last bars of a repeated passage. The first time, play the bars under bracket 1; after the repeat sign, skip them and play the bars under bracket 2 instead. Also called volta brackets.
